sections.executive_summary: Overnight reporting from Iranian territory recorded multiple missile launches — two from Omidiyeh toward the south, one from Behbahan, one from Jask and one from Sirik toward the Strait of Hormuz — alongside repeated UAV launches and jet activity over Shiraz, Isfahan and Kermanshah. In Gaza, Hamas's interior ministry said an Israeli strike on the Shati camp in Gaza City killed Muhammad Abu al-Awf, 47, director of internal security in the northern Gaza Strip, together with his wife and two teenage daughters, a day after the killing of apparatus chief Naim Abu Nahal. Lebanese channels logged 131 alerts on Wednesday, dominated by 68 UAV sightings and 39 artillery strikes concentrated in Nabatieh, Tyre and Marjayoun districts.

points: Missile launches were reported from four separate locations overnight: two missiles from Omidiyeh toward the south at 00:19 local (2049Z) in Khuzestan Province; another missile from Behbahan at 00:46 local (2116Z); a missile from Jask at 00:53 local (2123Z) in Hormozgan Province; and a missile from Sirik toward the Strait of Hormuz at 01:41 local (2211Z). All timestamps were carried on a 120-second delayed feed via FromIran. (Source: @shin_persian/12897)

UAV activity was concentrated in Khuzestan: at least three sounds of UAV launches were heard in Behbahan within a short period at 23:57 local (2027Z), and a subsequent compilation reported 'lots of UAV launches from Omidiyeh' alongside jet activity over southern and western Iran. No quantities were given for the Omidiyeh launches. (Source: @shin_persian/12895)

Jet activity was reported at three widely separated locations: over Shiraz in Fars Province at 23:58 local (2028Z), over Baharestan in Isfahan Province at 23:28 local (1958Z), and over Kermanshah in Kermanshah Province at 23:08 local (1938Z). The compilation message described jet activity over both southern and western Iran. (Source: @shin_persian/12896)

The same compilation stated that no blasts occurred on Qeshm island, that one to two blasts were heard in Sirik with the cause unclear as either a launch or a strike, and that a video received in connection with the Sirik incident was of doubtful authenticity and under verification. (Source: @shin_persian/12891)

Hamas's interior ministry said an Israeli strike on the Shati camp in Gaza City overnight killed Muhammad Abu al-Awf, 47, director of internal security in the northern Gaza Strip, along with his wife and two teenage daughters. The IDF had not commented on the strike at the time of reporting. (Source: @manniefabian/59582)

The strike came one day after the killing of Naim Abu Nahal, chief of Hamas's internal security apparatus, in an Israeli strike in Gaza City. The military subsequently stated that Abu Nahal belonged to a 'secret circle' in the group that held the body of Staff Sgt. Oron Shaul over the years. (Source: @manniefabian/59584)

Israeli warplanes were reported over southern Lebanon in a channel alert tagged with the Israeli warplanes marker, part of a sequence of alerts covering the southern border area. (Source: @redlinkleb/55081)
Israeli army detonations were reported at the outskirts of the town of Adaisseh al-Qusayr, listed among the day's explosion events in the Lebanese border belt. (Source: @redlinkleb/55112)

Illumination bombs were reported dropped over Talousa in southern Lebanon simultaneously with a machine-gun sweep, and separately over Houla and between Shaqra and Doubiyeh. (Source: @redlinkleb/55086)

The end-of-day Lebanese statistics attributed airstrikes to Markaba and Wadi al-Salouqi, and listed artillery fire on Mansouri (6), Mefdoun (5), Zibqin (4), Braashit (4), Khiam (3), Zawtar al-Sharqiya (3) and Shaqra (3), among other locations. (Source: @redlinkleb/55110)

Hamas's interior ministry announced that Muhammad Abu al-Awf, 47, director of internal security in the northern Gaza Strip, was killed in an Israeli strike on the Shati camp in Gaza City overnight, together with his wife and two teenage daughters. (Source: @manniefabian/59582)

The killing followed by one day the death of Naim Abu Nahal, chief of Hamas's internal security apparatus, who was killed in an Israeli strike in Gaza City. The two consecutive strikes removed the head of the apparatus and a senior director within it. (Source: @manniefabian/59584)

The Israeli military stated that Naim Abu Nahal was part of a 'secret circle' within Hamas that held the body of Staff Sgt. Oron Shaul over the years, linking the internal security apparatus to the retention of Israeli remains. (Source: @manniefabian/59584)
The IDF had not commented on the Shati camp strike at the time of the report, leaving the military's account of that specific incident unstated. (Source: @manniefabian/59582)

The end-of-day tally for Wednesday 25 November 2026 recorded 131 alerts, led by 68 UAV sightings and 39 artillery shelling alerts. Alerts concentrated in Nabatieh district (33), Tyre (31) and Marjayoun (23), with 76 in Nabatieh governorate; the most frequently named villages were Zibqin, Mansouri and Mefdoun with seven alerts each. (Source: @redlinkleb/55109)

The daily total fell by 12 alerts (8%) from the previous day's 143, but the weekly figure reached 423 alerts at a daily average of 141, up 39% over the same days the previous week. Since the start of November the cumulative total reached 3,044 alerts at a daily average of 122. (Source: @redlinkleb/55109)

Airstrikes were recorded on Markaba and Wadi al-Salouqi, while artillery fire was logged on Mansouri (6), Mefdoun (5), Zibqin (4), Braashit (4), Khiam (3), Zawtar al-Sharqiya (3), Shaqra (3), Wadi Zibqin (2), Wadi al-Salouqi (2), Haddatha (2), Kafr Tebnit (2), Kafr Shuba, Houla, Alman and Bani Hayyan. (Source: @redlinkleb/55110)

Detonations were reported at Aynata (2), Bint Jbeil, Zawtar al-Sharqiya, Qantara, Kafr Tebnit, Kounine and Markaba, with separate reports of army detonations at the outskirts of Adaisseh al-Qusayr. (Source: @redlinkleb/55110)

Machine-gun sweeps were recorded at Khiam (2), Mazraat Beit al-Siyad, Wadi al-Salouqi, Braashit and Talousa, with illumination bombs dropped over Talousa, over Houla and between Shaqra and Doubiyeh, and shelling plus sweeps directed from Houla toward Talousa. (Source: @redlinkleb/55098)

UAV sightings were most frequent over Jibsheet (4), Shoukin (4), Qana (4), Harouf (3) and Qabrikha (3), with the most active districts listed as Nabatieh (44), Tyre (44) and Marjayoun (26). (Source: @redlinkleb/55110)

Two claims were explicitly corrected: a circulated report of a war-remnants explosion in Nabatieh with two injuries, one critical, was declared incorrect, and a video purporting to show drones over Beirut was assessed as showing lights that 'are not as they appear'. (Source: @redlinkleb/55149)

No message in this batch reported any development in Syria or Iraq; channel traffic in the relevant period covered Lebanon, Gaza and Iran only, so no operational facts for these theatres can be stated. (Source: @redlinkleb/55110)

A missile was reported launched from Sirik toward the Strait of Hormuz at 01:41 local time (2211Z) in Hormozgan Province, the only launch in the batch explicitly oriented toward the Strait. (Source: @shin_persian/12904)
A separate missile launch was reported from Jask in Hormozgan Province at 00:53 local time (2123Z), on the Gulf of Oman approaches to the Strait. (Source: @shin_persian/12903)

The overnight compilation stated there were no blasts on Qeshm island, the large island inside the Strait of Hormuz, while one to two blasts were heard at Sirik on the mainland coast. (Source: @shin_persian/12891)

The Hormozgan launches occurred within roughly an hour of the Khuzestan launches from Omidiyeh and Behbahan, indicating near-simultaneous activity across two southern Iranian provinces bordering Gulf waters. (Source: @shin_persian/12900)

sections.threat_assessment: The overnight pattern shows dispersed launch activity across at least four Iranian locations — Omidiyeh and Behbahan in Khuzestan, and Jask and Sirik in Hormozgan — with one launch explicitly oriented toward the Strait of Hormuz and simultaneous UAV and jet activity over Fars, Isfahan and Kermanshah. The absence of any stated impact, interception or attribution in the source reporting means the intended targets and effects remain unconfirmed, and the Sirik blasts were explicitly described as of unclear cause with a video of doubtful authenticity under verification. In Gaza, two consecutive strikes removed the chief of Hamas's internal security apparatus and a senior director within it, an attrition pattern against the body the Israeli military links to the retention of Staff Sgt. Oron Shaul's remains. In Lebanon, the 131-alert day with 68 UAV sightings and 39 artillery alerts, and a 39% week-on-week rise in daily averages, indicates sustained rather than episodic pressure along the Nabatieh–Tyre–Marjayoun belt.
sections.regional_response: The most concrete external response in the batch is the reported RAF move to install Kevlar anti-drone netting over exposed aircraft at bases, cited against both Russian sabotage and Iran-linked drone threats and described as a tactic first employed in the Ukraine war. No message records an official Israeli statement on the Iranian launches, and the IDF had not commented on the Shati camp strike at the time of reporting. Lebanese channels issued two corrections rather than escalatory claims — rejecting a reported war-remnants explosion with two injuries in Nabatieh and assessing a 'drones over Beirut' video as showing lights that are not as they appear. The Iranian launch reporting itself carries a 120-second transmission delay via the FromIran feed, which constrains real-time corroboration.
sections.intelligence_notes: Collection in this batch is heavily weighted toward two open-source feeds: delayed incident reports from Iran (shin_persian, all posts marked with a 120-second delay via FromIran) and Lebanese alert aggregation (redlinkleb), with Gaza sourcing resting on a single Israeli military-affairs channel citing Hamas's interior ministry. The Iranian reporting is observational only — launch sounds, jet noise and blast reports — with no stated weapon types beyond 'missile' and 'UAV', no ranges and no damage assessment, and one compilation explicitly flags an unverified video. The Lebanese statistics provide the most quantifiable picture, with per-village artillery counts, detonation sites and a 3,044-alert cumulative total since the start of November. No reporting in this batch covers Syria or Iraq, and no message attributes the Iranian launches to a stated target or order of battle.
